open_points.subject: replacement account after a lost password
open_points.text: “an administrator may disable that account and create a new one” alongside “mandatory unique normalized email as login identifier”
open_points.question: Can the replacement account use the disabled account’s email, and if so, what releases or transfers that unique identifier?
options: Disabled accounts retain their email uniqueness, so the replacement must use another email.
Disabling an account releases its email for reuse.
The administrator must first move the old account to another email through the recovery override, then create the replacement.
open_points.default_guess: Disabled accounts retain the unique email; the administrator must move the old account to another email before reusing it.

witness.initial: A staff account owns normalized email staff@example.com, is active, and its holder has lost the password.
events: The administrator creates the promised replacement account for the same holder using staff@example.com.
outcomes: Creation is rejected because the disabled account still owns the unique email.
Creation succeeds because disabling the old account released the email.
witness.observer: The administrator and the staff holder

open_points.subject: email-verified mark lifecycle
open_points.text: “A staff account keeps a recorded ‘email verified’ mark: the administrator's activation, the first administrator's creation (R0-07) and the recovery override (R0-20) set it”
open_points.question: What value does the mark have when an administrator creates a pending staff account, before activation?
options: The mark is absent or null until activation.
The mark is already true despite the account remaining pending.
open_points.default_guess: The mark is false on creation and becomes true on activation.

witness.initial: An administrator is authorized to create staff accounts.
events: The administrator creates a pending staff account.
The administrator reads the account before activating it.
outcomes: The account view reports email_verified=null or true.

open_points.subject: visibility of the email-verified mark
open_points.question: Which principal may obtain this account view, through what product action, and what failure is returned to principals that may not view it?
options: Only administrators viewing managed staff accounts see the mark.
Each staff holder can view the mark on their own account.
Both administrators and the account holder can view it.
open_points.default_guess: Only an administrator’s staff-account detail view exposes the mark.

witness.initial: An active operator and an active administrator exist, and the operator’s mark is set.
events: The operator requests their own account information.
The administrator requests the operator’s account information.
outcomes: Only the administrator receives a view containing the mark.
Both principals receive a view containing the mark.

open_points.subject: sole-administrator host recovery
open_points.text: “a sole administrator's loss stays the host-level operation of R0-20” and “such a recovery stays a host-level operation outside the product”
open_points.question: What named host actor and operation perform this recovery, what inputs and stored facts may they change, what observable success and failure outcomes exist, and where is the host/product trust boundary?
options: A supported local command changes credentials on the existing administrator account.
The host operator performs a direct database repair under an operational procedure.
No supported recovery action exists; restoration is deployment-specific.
open_points.default_guess: A local host-only command repairs the existing administrator using non-argument secret input and explicit exit outcomes.

witness.initial: Exactly one administrator account exists, and its holder has lost both its login email and password.
events: The host operator attempts the recovery that R0-23 says remains available.
outcomes: A defined host command updates the existing account and reports a branchable success or failure.
There is no defined command, so the operator must edit storage directly or choose an implementation-specific procedure.
witness.observer: The host operator and the administrator
